pageSubtitle: Everything you need to know about Montreux and making the most of your trip

items.name: By Air
items.description:
Geneva (GVA) is the recommended airport, with Montreux just 1h30 by train or 1 hour by car.

If you can't get a direct flight to Geneva, Zurich (ZRH) is Switzerland's main hub. Trains from Zurich to Montreux take about 2 hours through the heart of Switzerland.
items.tip: Book flights and trains in advance — Geneva fills up quickly during peak season.

items.name: By Train
items.description:
Switzerland's trains are the best way to reach Montreux — punctual, scenic, and stress-free. From Geneva Airport, take a direct train to Montreux (no transfers needed). Journey time is about 1 hour 30 minutes with beautiful views of the lake and vineyards along the way. The Fairmont is a 5-minute walk from Montreux station.

Important: tickets must be purchased before boarding — buy in the SBB app or at station ticket counters.
items.tip: A Swiss Travel Pass gives unlimited train travel — great value if you're exploring Switzerland before or after the wedding.

items.name: By Car or Ride Share
items.description: It's approximately a 1 hour drive from Geneva Airport to Montreux, following the A1 and A9 highways along the lake. Rental cars are available at the airport. Uber also operates in Geneva and Montreux if you'd prefer not to drive.

items.name: Montreux Riviera Promenade
items.description: Just steps from the Fairmont, this lakeside path is lined with vibrant flowers and palm trees, offering sweeping views of Lake Geneva and the Alps. The promenade stretches several kilometres from Clarens to Villeneuve — perfect for a morning jog, leisurely walk, or sunset stroll. The famous Freddie Mercury statue is along the way.
items.tip: May is peak blooming season — perfect for photos with the Alps reflecting on the lake.

items.name: Rochers de Naye
items.description: Take the cogwheel train from Montreux station up to 2,042m for panoramic views over Lake Geneva and the Alps. At the top you'll find hiking trails, alpine gardens, and marmots!
items.tip: Sit on the right side going up for the best lake views. About 55 minutes from Montreux.

items.name: Narcissus Hikes
items.description: From late May to early June, the hills above Montreux are blanketed in blooming narcissus flowers — a local phenomenon known as "May Snow." Beautiful trails at Les Pléiades and Les Avants offer some of the best views of this fleeting sight.
items.tip: Trail conditions vary — ask the Fairmont concierge for up-to-date route recommendations.

items.name: Glacier 3000
items.description: Head to Glacier 3000 near Les Diablerets — about 1.5 hours from Montreux. Reachable by cable car, with spectacular views of Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn, year-round snow, and the Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks.
items.tip: Dress warmly even in summer. Short hikes and snow activities available year-round.
items.address: Col du Pillon, 1865 Les Diablerets, Switzerland

items.name: Château de Chillon
items.description:
Switzerland's most visited castle, right on the edge of Lake Geneva. Medieval architecture, historic rooms, dungeons, and picturesque courtyards — immortalised by Lord Byron.

Walk: ~45 min from the Fairmont along the promenade
Train: Montreux → Veytaux-Chillon (2 min, ~15 min total)
Open daily 9am–7pm (last entry 6pm) · CHF 13

items.name: Château d'Aigle
items.description:
A medieval castle housing a fascinating wine museum — a great pairing with a Lavaux wine tour.

Train: Montreux → Aigle (10 min, ~30 min total)
Tue–Sun 10am–5pm, closed Mon · CHF 12

items.name: Lavaux Vineyards (UNESCO)
items.description: Terraced vineyards along the hillsides above Lake Geneva — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Accessible by train, car, or on foot between the villages of Cully, Epesses, and Saint-Saphorin.
items.tip: Hop aboard the Lavaux Express or Lavaux Panoramic — tourist trains winding through the vineyards with stops for tastings.

items.name: Wine Tasting
items.description: Family-run domaines specialising in Chasselas — a crisp, mineral-rich white wine native to the area. Most require reservations, especially on weekends.
items.tip: Book ahead — same-day tastings are rarely available at the best estates.

items.name: Lake Geneva by Boat
items.description: The CGN (Compagnie Générale de Navigation) offers elegant cruises on Lake Geneva with a stop in Montreux — a beautiful way to spend an afternoon.
items.tip: Perfect for a leisurely day trip or a memorable arrival on the lake.

items.name: Montreux Tennis Club
items.description:
Outdoor red clay courts with lake views, open to visitors of all levels.

Court rental: CHF 60/hr · Coaching: CHF 100/hr
30 min walk along the promenade · Train: Montreux → Territet (2 min)

items.name: Fairmont — Pools & Hot Tub
items.description: Outdoor and heated indoor pool plus a hot tub, all with panoramic mountain views. Located on floor -1 of the Fairmont.
items.tip: A perfect way to unwind between wedding events.

items.name: Fairmont — Spa & Gym
items.description: Sauna, steam room, jacuzzi, spa treatments, and a fully equipped gym with fitness classes. Located on floor -1 of the Fairmont.
items.tip: Book spa treatments in advance — they fill up quickly.

items.name: Day Trip to Lausanne
items.description: A vibrant Swiss city just 30 minutes by train. Highlights: Gothic cathedral, Olympic Museum, the charming Old Town, and the lakefront at Ouchy.
items.tip: The Olympic Museum is world-class and right on the lake — worth a few hours.

items.name: GoldenPass Panoramic Train
items.description: One of Switzerland's most iconic train journeys — starting in Montreux and winding through the Alps toward Gstaad. Panoramic windows and plush seating with breathtaking mountain views.
items.tip: Book panoramic seats in advance. The stretch from Montreux to Zweisimmen is especially dramatic.

items.name: Sleepy Bear Coffee
items.description: Montreux's premier specialty coffee shop — the perfect place to start your day with expertly crafted espresso and a welcoming atmosphere.

items.name: Confiserie Zurcher
items.description: A traditional Swiss confectionery and café — perfect for breakfast pastries, hot chocolate, and handmade chocolates to take home.
items.tip: Pick up a box of Swiss chocolates as a souvenir — made in-house.

items.name: Montreux Jazz Café
items.description: Lively vibes and modern European cuisine inspired by the legendary Montreux Jazz Festival. Located at the Fairmont.

items.name: La Terrasse
items.description: Elegant Mediterranean-inspired dining at the Fairmont with beautiful views of Lake Geneva — perfect for a romantic dinner.

items.name: Funky Claude's Bar
items.description: Casual cocktails, light bites, and a comfort-food menu with a fun, jazzy atmosphere at the Fairmont. Live music most evenings.
items.tip: Named after legendary Montreux Jazz Festival founder Claude Nobs — a Montreux icon.

items.name: La Rouvenaz
items.description: A charming local favorite right on the lakeside — known for fresh seafood and Swiss specialties with beautiful lake views.

items.name: Michelin Dining in Lausanne
items.description: If you have extra time, a quick 30-minute train ride to Lausanne opens up several world-class Michelin-starred restaurants for a truly special meal.

items.name: Currency
items.description: Switzerland uses Swiss Francs (CHF).

items.name: Language
items.description: Montreux is in French-speaking Switzerland. French is the main language, but English is widely spoken in hotels, restaurants, and tourist areas.
items.tip: 'Merci' (thank you), 'Bonjour' (hello), 'S'il vous plaît' (please) — locals appreciate the effort!

items.name: Weather in May
items.description: May in Montreux is beautiful spring weather: 59–72°F on warm days. Expect occasional rain — pack a light waterproof jacket.
items.tip: May is peak blooming season — the lake promenade will be stunning with roses and flowers.

items.name: Plug Adaptor
items.description: Switzerland uses Type J sockets, which are unique to Switzerland. A universal travel adaptor will cover this.
items.tip: Don't forget — EU adaptors don't always fit Swiss sockets!

items.name: Emergency Numbers
items.description: Police: 117 | Ambulance: 144 | Fire: 118. The nearest hospital is RSMR in Vevey, about 5km from Montreux.

items.name: Montreux Riviera Card
items.description: Many hotels provide guests with a Montreux Riviera Card, which includes free or discounted travel on local buses, boats, and mountain railways throughout the region.
items.tip: Ask your hotel at check-in — it can save you a lot on local transport.
